name: OH-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean (R+17) in an Appalachian Ohio seat
Incumbent Michael Rulli running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Democratic challenger Elizabeth Kirtley has raised only about $1,100
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at roughly 4 percent
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Rulli: a deep-red district, first-term incumbency, and a fundraising gap of roughly a thousand to one, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting any competitive threat. Markets agree, pricing Kirtley's chances near 4 percent.
model.watch: Any sign of Democratic outside spending or polling putting the race in single digits would warrant revisiting, but nothing currently indicates that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This southeastern Ohio seat is among the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+17. Michael Rulli, first elected in 2024, is running for a second term and holds every structural advantage: incumbency, name recognition from his Senate-adjacent profile, and a dominant fundraising position, with more than $1.1 million raised against roughly $1,100 for Democrat Elizabeth Kirtley.

No public general-election polling exists for the race, and no major expert raters list it as competitive. Prediction markets give Kirtley about a 4 percent chance of winning. Barring an unexpected external shock, the seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands.
